description:
FOUND s509 (Fable, 2026-10-06) by the review probes for s507p (perf round 39); PRE-EXISTING on main fee16466.

REPRODUCERS (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/p39/ap2.pl (answers beside it: ap2.perl / ap2.main / ap2.tree; perl 5.40.3, main fee16466, the s507p tree b74d4938), rows 17 / 34 for `+=`, rows 6 / 7 / 23 / 24 for `.=`):
  my @a = (10, 20); my $i = 0; $a[$i] += ++$i; print "@a\n";                      perl: 11 20     PCL: 10 11
  my %h = (a => 1, b => 2); my $key = "a"; $h{$key} += ($key = "b") ? 5 : 0;        perl: a=6 b=2   PCL: a=1 b=6
  my @l = ("one \\", "two"); my $i = 0; $l[$i] .= $l[++$i];                        (join a continuation line: perl appends to l[0])

WHAT PERL DOES: for `PLACE OP= VALUE` the place's operands (the container, the index or key) are evaluated first, left to
right and ONCE; then VALUE; then the element's current value is read, combined and stored back into THAT element.
WHAT PCL DOES on main: reads the element with the index as it is before VALUE, evaluates VALUE, then evaluates the index
AGAIN for the store -- so the result lands in a different element than the one that was read.

STATE: s507p (round 39) rewrote the lowering of `.=` (its M4(c)): there a CALL operand is evaluated once and before the
value, and the review asked it (finding F1) to bind a VARIABLE index / key before the value as well.  This task is the
SIBLING operators (`+=` `-=` `*=` `/=` `**=` `%=` `x=` `&=` `|=` `^=` `<<=` `>>=` `||=` `&&=` `//=`), which that batch does
not touch unless one helper serves them all.  #1152 (completed) fixed the DOUBLE evaluation of a call key for a flat
element; this is the ORDER for a plain variable operand, which #1152's rows do not cover.

FIX DIRECTION (rule 11): one place-binding helper for every compound assignment -- the one `.=` gets in s507p -- which
binds an index / key to a temporary when the right side is anything but a literal or a plain variable read, so the common
shapes (`$h{$k} += 1`, `$a[$i] .= $x`, `$n{$w}++`) emit what they emit today.  Bar: corpus-diff explained per file,
the bench rows arrhash / arrhash-k / intloop+= unchanged.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (taken): the two reproducers above on main and on the s507p tree -- identical wrong
answers for `+=` on both, so the `.=` rewrite did not reach the other operators.

NOT MATCHABLE, for the record (rows 12 / 13 / 29 / 30 of the probe): a right side that DELETES the element or REPLACES
the whole array -- perl appends to the detached element, so the hash stays empty; with raw elements PCL re-creates it.

PRIORITY: low-medium (silent wrong, rare spelling; the continuation-line idiom is the realistic one).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a compound assignment reads a VARIABLE index / key AFTER its right side -- `$a[$i] += ++$i` stores into a[1] what it read from a[0] (perl: a[0] += 1); the same for `-=` `*=` `x=` `||=` ... and `$h{$key} OP= ($key = ...)`; `$lines[$i] .= $lines[++$i]` is the ordinary spelling
